newsitem.title: UK: NatWest down further after analyst briefing.
newsitem.headline: NatWest down further after analyst briefing.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc shares extended their early loss by midsession on Tuesday as an analyst briefing failed to improve the cautious response to the bank's first-half results, dealers said.
The stock was down 30p at 840 by 1044 GMT in heavy volume of 7.6 million shares.

"Basically there wasn't really any new direction over and above what has already been announced and the shares had been hoping for some new impetus," said one leading analyst, who asked not to be named.
"And they are not showing the growth that other retail banks are."
The post-results decline in NatWest shares stands in stark contrast with recent sharp gains in HSBC Holdings and Lloyds TSB Plc, both of whose profits beat analyst expectations.
Banking specialists said one negative from today's results statement was that NatWest had failed to set specific new targets such as in its cost-income ratio.
"The results were fine as far as they went, but unfortunately NatWest has a huge credibility gap to bridge," said one senior dealer.
"What was needed to change sentiment was that they needed to be more specific in terms of their targets and when they intend to reach them."
However, he said, there may not be much more downside in NatWest shares. "At the end of the day this is not a completely beaten-up player."
Earlier, NatWest shares fell from the outset as its first-half results failed to provide any positive surprise.
"There is nothing in the figures to suggest any further black holes...but I can't see anything sparkling in there," said a dealer at one top investment bank.

Dogged in recent months by losses in derivatives trading at its NatWest Markets unit, NatWest shares have underperformed other banks which have focused more on expanding their domestic retail operations where profits have soared.
The company's pre-tax profit on continuing operations, excluding a charge of 106 million stg, rose 17 percent to 775 million stg from 662 million a year before.
Analyst forecasts had been mostly in a range between 757 million stg and 770 million.
The interim dividend was raised 10.4 percent to 10.6p, matching forecasts.

In line with its previous statements, NatWest said its treasury business would become a separate sector while its NatWest Markets unit would be "taken forward under new leadership on a clearly focused basis with close regard to profitability".
By 1123 GMT, NatWest shares were down 36p, or 4.1 percent, at 834, the biggest decliner in the FTSE 100 index.
